docs.title: A-Z Bias-Variance Tradeoff Tutorial Series
docs.text:
Welcome to the A-Z Bias-Variance Tradeoff Tutorial Series, designed specifically for Advanced Machine Learning Engineers.

This tutorial series explores the core statistical mechanics, empirical risk behavior, penalty trajectories, cross-validation variance, dimensional effects, ensemble decomposition, and temporal complexity involved in machine learning model evaluation and optimization.

docs.title: Series Outline
docs.text:
1. 01. Mathematical Error Decomposition Mathematical decomposition of expected prediction error into Bias, Variance, and Irreducible Noise. Practical estimation using bootstrapping and k-NN proxies.

  2. 02. Model Complexity & Polynomials Visualizing the classic tradeoff via polynomial regression, condition numbers of design matrices, SVD analysis, and interpolation thresholds.

  3. 03. Learning Curves & Sample Complexity Empirical Risk vs. True Risk, sample complexity bounds, VC-dimension context, and confidence interval bands across training set scaling.

  4. 04. Penalty-Based Control (Regularization) Ridge, Lasso, Elastic Net, Bayesian priors (Laplace vs Gaussian), LARS/Coordinate Descent paths, and exact shrinkage trajectories.

  5. 05. Cross-Validation Strategies Assessment variance, LOOCV, Nested CV, Nadeau & Bengio variance corrections, and Block Time-Series splitting.

  6. 06. Feature Selection & Dimensionality Curse of dimensionality, Filter/Wrapper methods, RFE, Stability selection via randomized Lasso, PCA vs. PLS variance mechanics.

  7. 07. Aggregation & Ensembles Variance reduction in Random Forests vs. Bias reduction in Gradient Boosting Machines (GBM) and Histogram-based boosting.

  8. 08. Temporally Complex Models Bias-variance tradeoff in time-series (VAR, ARIMA), stationarity impact, lag-length optimization, and expanding/rolling window CV.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Decomposition of Expected Prediction Error into Bias^2, Variance, and Irreducible Noise (\(\sigma^2\)):

\[ \mathbb{E}[(y - \hat{f}(x))^2] = \text{Bias}[\hat{f}(x)]^2 + \text{Var}[\hat{f}(x)] + \sigma^2 \]
